exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 Which Language Will You Choose
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Lily: Have you decided which foreign language to take next year, Tom?
Tom: I'm thinking about Spanish. So many people around the world speak it.
Lily: That's a good reason. What made you interested in the first place?
Tom: Last month I watched a Spanish film and loved how the language sounded.
Lily: I know what you mean. I want to learn Japanese myself.
Tom: Japanese? Why is that?
Lily: I love Japanese stories, and I'd like to read them in the original language.
Tom: That's great. Learning any new language opens a door to another world.
exercises.translation_cn: Lily 问 Tom 明年选哪门外语;Tom 想学西班牙语,因为说的人多;他上个月看了部西班牙电影,喜欢那语言的声音;Lily 想学日语,因为喜欢日本故事,想读原文;Tom 说学任何新语言都会打开通往另一个世界的门。

questions.stem: Which language is Tom thinking of taking?

options: His teacher chose it for him.
He watched a film and loved how it sounded.

questions.stem: Which language does Lily want to learn?
Why does Lily want to learn it?
options: She wants to read Japanese stories in the original.
She is moving abroad next week.
Her parents made her choose it.

questions.stem: What does Tom say about learning a new language?
options: It is mostly a waste of time.
It opens a door to another world.

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 Languages in Australia
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Long ago, hundreds of different languages were spoken across Australia.
Today only a small number of them are still used every day.
Europeans arrived a little over two hundred years ago, and many languages slowly died out.
For Aboriginal communities, language is a central part of who they are.
It links them to their land, their history, and their sense of belonging.
exercises.translation_cn: 很久以前,澳大利亚有数百种不同的语言;如今只有少数仍在日常使用;欧洲人两百多年前到来,许多语言渐渐消亡;对原住民社区来说,语言是他们身份的核心;它把他们与土地、历史和归属感相连。

questions.stem: About how many languages were once spoken in Australia?
How many of them are still used daily now?
When did Europeans arrive, according to the talk?
options: A little over two hundred years ago.

questions.stem: What is language for Aboriginal communities?
options: A central part of their identity.

questions.stem: What does their language link them to?
options: Their land, history, and sense of belonging.

exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 Two Words for Blue
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Anna: Look at these two squares. Are they the same colour or different?
Igor: Different, of course. One is light blue and the other is dark blue.
Anna: Really? To me they both look just 'blue'.
Igor: In Russian we have two separate words, so I notice the line between them at once.
Anna: That's amazing. So your language trains your eyes a little.
Igor: Maybe. Scientists say Russian speakers are faster at telling these blues apart.
Anna: I'd never have guessed that words could change how quickly we see.
Igor: It shows how deeply language and the mind are connected.
exercises.translation_cn: Anna 让 Igor 看两个方块是否同色;Igor 说不同,一个浅蓝一个深蓝;Anna 觉得两个都只是'蓝';Igor 说俄语里有两个分开的词,所以一眼就看出界线;Anna 惊叹语言训练了眼睛;Igor 说研究表明俄语者更快区分这些蓝色;两人感叹语言与思维联系之深。

questions.stem: How do the two squares look to Anna?
options: They look like two different reds.

questions.stem: Why does Igor notice the difference at once?
options: Russian has two separate words for the blues.

questions.stem: What do scientists say about Russian speakers?
options: They cannot see the colour blue.
They tell these blues apart faster.

questions.stem: What surprises Anna about words?
options: That words have no meaning at all.
That blue is her favourite colour.
That Russian is very easy to learn.
That words can change how quickly we see.

questions.stem: What does the talk show, according to Igor?
options: Language and the mind are deeply connected.

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 A Healthier Brain
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Speaking two languages does more than help you talk to more people.
Every time you switch between them, your brain gets a small workout.
Studies show that this effort can keep the mind sharp for longer.
It may even delay certain memory problems by several years.
So learning a language is not only useful; it is good for the brain.
exercises.translation_cn: 会说两种语言不只是能和更多人交流;每次在两种语言间切换,大脑都会做个小锻炼;研究表明这种努力能让头脑更久保持敏锐;甚至可能把某些记忆问题推迟数年;所以学语言不仅有用,还有益大脑。

questions.stem: What happens each time you switch languages?
options: Your brain gets a small workout.

questions.stem: What do the studies show?
options: The effort can keep the mind sharp for longer.

questions.stem: What may speaking two languages delay?

options: Languages are a waste of time.

exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 Saving Grandpa's Dialect
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mei: My grandpa speaks an old dialect that almost no young people use now.
Sam: That's a pity. What happens when the last speakers are gone?
Mei: A lot of stories and local knowledge could disappear with them.
Sam: So have you thought of doing anything about it?
Mei: Yes. Every weekend I record him telling old tales in his dialect.
Sam: That's a wonderful idea. You're saving more than just words.
Mei: Exactly. The real question is whether my generation will keep it alive.
Sam: I'm sure small efforts like yours can make a real difference.
exercises.translation_cn: Mei 说爷爷讲一种几乎没年轻人用的老方言;Sam 觉得可惜,问最后的说话者走后会怎样;Mei 说许多故事和地方知识可能随之消失;Mei 每个周末录爷爷用方言讲老故事;Sam 称赞这是在拯救不止是词语的东西;Mei 说真正的问题是她这代人能否让它存续;Sam 相信小小的努力能带来真正的改变。

questions.stem: What is special about Mei's grandpa's dialect?
options: Everyone in the city speaks it.

questions.stem: What could disappear with the last speakers?

options: She records him telling old tales.

questions.stem: What does Sam say she is really saving?
What does Mei call the real question?
options: How old the dialect really is.
Whether her generation will keep it alive.

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 Why You Think the Way You Do
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: We have seen that speakers of different languages can think in different ways.
But this talk is not really about how people far away think.
It is about how you, yourself, think every single day.
Your language quietly shapes what you notice and what you forget.
So it is always worth asking why you see the world the way you do.
exercises.translation_cn: 我们看到说不同语言的人可能以不同方式思考;但这次演讲并非真的关于远方的人如何思考;而是关于你自己每天如何思考;你的语言悄悄塑造你注意什么、忽略什么;所以值得问问:你为何这样看世界。

questions.stem: What have we seen about speakers of different languages?
options: They all think exactly the same.
They can think in different ways.

questions.stem: What is this talk really about?
What does your language quietly shape?
options: What you notice and what you forget.

questions.stem: How often does language shape your thinking?
What does the speaker say is worth asking?
options: Why you see the world as you do.
